newsitem.title: JAPAN: Majority in Japan coalition seek extra budget - MP.
newsitem.headline: Majority in Japan coalition seek extra budget - MP.

text.p: A majority in Japan's ruling coalition think Japan must announce a supplementary budget with additional public spending this year, a senior coalition official told reporters on Thursday.

Asked about the likelihood of an extra budget aimed at stimulating the economy this fiscal year, Koichi Kato, secretary-general of the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) said: "The point is that a lot of people in the governing party think the economy has not had real energy yet so we should at least announce that we should have a supplementary budget with some public investment in it.
"In my party, the voice supporting a supplementary budget with public spending is very, very strong," Kato said. The LDP is the biggest partner in Japan's three-way coalition.
But Kato added the Social Democratic Party, the second biggest coalition force, has a different view about additional public spending and its effect on the economy.

Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and Finance Minister Wataru Kubo are expected to make a decision on whether to draft a supplementary budget after Japan's gross domestic product data is released on Friday.
